structured_output.hypothesis: In 2D sections of real plant tissue, the three wall segments at triple junctions meet at angles whose mean is 120° with small spread, and the deviation of each angle from 120° does not depend on the size difference of the adjoining cells, which only changes wall curvature.
structured_output.pass_criterion: From at least 500 triple junctions in xy-sections of ground-truth label volumes: (a) median of the three junction angles in [115°,125°], with at least 70% of all individual angles within 120±20°, using chords of the walls measured 2-3 µm from the junction; (b) at least 90% of junctions are three-way, with four-way junctions below 10%; (c) the absolute Spearman correlation between a junction's maximum deviation from 120° and the log ratio of largest to smallest adjoining cell cross-section area is below 0.3.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if any of the following holds: median junction angle outside [110°,130°]; fewer than 50% of angles within 120±20°; four-way or higher junctions exceed 25% of junctions; or the absolute Spearman correlation between maximum deviation from 120° and log cell-area ratio is 0.5 or higher with p<0.01, meaning cell size does change the junction angles.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'cell-walls meeting by threes at 120°' is read as the angle between wall tangents or short chords at a triple junction in a 2D section. 'Irrespective of size' means junction-angle deviation is uncorrelated with the cell-size ratio. 'Curvature determined by relative size' is not tested separately. Modern reinterpretation: sections are xy-planes of 3D confocal or light-sheet volumes with human-corrected cell instance labels. Junctions are pixels where three label IDs meet. Caveats: real walls are stiff, so 120° may hold only approximately; image anisotropy and segmentation artefacts must be controlled by using only the high-resolution xy plane.

dataset.name: Accurate and versatile 3D segmentation of plant tissues at cellular resolution: Core Datasets
dataset.publisher: Open Science Framework (OSF), Wolny et al. / Kreshuk and Hamprecht groups and collaborators
dataset.why_it_fits: Gives HDF5 volumes of fixed and live plant organs (Arabidopsis ovules, lateral root primordia) imaged by confocal and light-sheet microscopy. Each volume has a 'label' array of uint16 ground-truth cell instance IDs. Taking xy slices of the label array and finding pixels where three label IDs meet gives triple-junction angles. Cell areas from the same labels give size ratios.
